title: Cuttack: questions to carry into the city
scope_notice: This online reading accompanies the journey chapters below. Saved journey companions retain their existing chapters; this exposition is not included in downloads.

paragraphs.text: A useful journey can begin with a question small enough to follow. Instead of asking an object to represent an entire city, ask what can be known about this particular thing: how it was used, what it is made of, who made it, and which record supports the answer. Those questions need not all have answers.

The Fitzwilliam Museum records a flower-shaped gold filigree brooch made to order in Cuttack in 1952. It has a pin and a loop for use as a pendant; its maker is unknown. Material, function and maker are separate questions—even in one catalogued object. This record does not identify the photographed object below.

Try separating a description from an explanation. You can note the shape you see before deciding what it means. Then ask what evidence would help: a maker’s account, a label, a dated record or a closer look. If two descriptions disagree, retain the disagreement rather than choosing the more attractive answer.

Use the chapters below as different invitations to look and ask, not as proof that everything can be visited in one outing. Choose the question that interests you most and arrange the practical details around it. A saved journey keeps your choices together; it does not confirm an appointment or settle an object’s history.
